items.name: Using the Gemini API in a Chrome Extension.
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use the Gemini Cloud API in a Chrome Extension.

items.name: On-device AI with Gemini Nano
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use the Gemini Nano prompt API in Chrome Extensions. To learn more about the API, head over to Built-in AI on developer.chrome.com.

items.name: Ai.Gemini On Device Alt Texter
items.summary: Ai.Gemini On Device Alt Texter

items.name: Audio-Scribe: Transcribe audio messages with Chrome's multimodal Prompt API
items.summary: Audio-Scribe: Transcribe audio messages with Chrome's multimodal Prompt API

items.name: Calendar Mate: On-device AI with Gemini Nano
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use Chrome's built-in Prompt API in an extension to extract calendar event details from natural language text. To learn more about the API, see Prompt API on developer.chrome.com.

items.name: On-device Summarization with Gemini Nano
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use Chrome's built-in Summarizer API to generate AI-powered summaries of web pages directly on the user's device. The summarization runs entirely locally using Gemini Nano, ensuring privacy and fast performance without requiring an internet connection or API keys.

items.name: Cookbook - File Handling
items.summary: This sample demonstrates file handling in an extension.

items.name: geolocation via content script
items.summary: This recipe shows how to get geolocation access within a [content script][5]

items.name: geolocation via offscreen document
items.summary: This recipe shows how to get geolocation access within a service worker

items.name: geolocation inside a popup
items.summary: This recipe shows how to get geolocation access within a popup

items.name: Cookbook.Offscreen Clipboard Write
items.summary: This recipe shows how to write a string to the system clipboard using the [Offscreen document][1].

items.name: Cookbook.Offscreen Dom
items.summary: This recipe shows how to use DOMParser in an Extension Service Worker using the [Offscreen document][1].

items.name: Cookbook.Offscreen User Media
items.summary: This recipe shows how to record microphone audio with getUserMedia() in an [offscreen document][1].

items.name: permissions.addHostAccessRequest() Demo
items.summary: This sample demonstrates using the permissions.addHostAccessRequest API to request access to a host.

items.name: Service worker with push notification
items.summary: This sample demonstrates using the Push API with self.registration.pushManager.subscribe() and specifically how to use userVisibleOnly to silence required notifications when receiving a push message in a service worker based extension.

items.name: Global Side panel example
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to display the same side panel on every site using the Side Panel API.

items.name: Multiple side panels example
items.summary: You can use sidepanel.getOptions() to retrieve the current side panel and switch between side panels. This example sets a welcome side panel when the extension is first installed, then when the user navigates to a different tab, it replaces it with the main side panel.

items.name: Opening the side panel through a user interaction
items.summary: This example demonstrates using chrome.sidePanel.open() to open a global side panel through a context menu click and a tab-specific side panel by clicking a button in an extension page or a button click injected by a content script. This feature will be available starting Chrome 116.

items.name: Site-specific side panel example
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to display the side panel only on google.com using the Side Panel API. It also allows users to open the side panel by clicking on the action icon or a keyboard shortcut.

items.name: Using WASM as a module in Manifest V3
items.summary: This recipe shows how to use WASM in Manifest V3.

items.name: Using WASM in Manifest V3
items.summary: This recipe shows how to use WASM in Manifest V3.

items.name: Using XHR in Service Workers
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use code that relies on XHR within a extension's background service worker.

items.name: Reference.Mv3 Content Scripts
items.summary: Sample code for the [Executing arbitrary strings][section] section of the MV3 migration documentation.

items.name: Bookmarks Manager
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use the chrome.bookmarks API to search, add, edit, and delete bookmarks.

items.name: Catifier
items.summary: When the extension is enabled, it replaces every image of extension jpg or jpeg, with this image.

items.name: Sample CO₂ Meter Chrome Extension
items.summary: The extension uses WebHID to access a device for measuring the CO₂ level and temperature in your surroundings.

items.name: chrome.declarativeNetRequest - No Cookies Rule Manager
items.summary: This sample demonstrates using the chrome.declarativeNetRequest API to remove the Cookie header from requests matching custom URL filters.

items.name: Sample.Favicon Cs
items.summary: This example fetches the favicon from www.google.com and inserts it at the top left of Google search pages.

items.name: Demo
items.summary: Clicking this extension's action button while viewing a Chromium code review will open a small popup that shows what (if any) Chromium version the review was merged into.

items.name: Sample.Optional Permissions
items.summary: This sample extension changes the New Tab page, prompting the user for permission to display their top sites. It demonstrates how extensions can provide users with the option to enable additional features.

items.name: Page Redder
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use the chrome.action API to execute code when the extension icon is clicked.

items.name: Dictionary Side panel example
items.summary: This example allows users to right-click on a word and see the definition on the side panel using the Side Panel API.

items.name: chrome.tabCapture recorder
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use the chrome.tabCapture API to record in the background, using a service worker and offscreen document.

items.name: Text Replacer
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how an extension can replace text on a page in response to user invocation.

items.name: Sample Chrome Theme
items.summary: This is a Chrome theme, that shows a number of color customization options.

items.name: Drink Water Alarm
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to use the Alarms API and Notifications API to remind users to drink water at set intervals.

items.name: WebGPU extension sample
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to use the WebGPU API to generate a red triangle using an extension service worker.

items.name: Tutorial.Broken Color
items.summary: This is a simple sample extension used in the [Debugging extensions][1] tutorial. The purpose of this extension is to demonstrate how to debug different extension components. This extension changes the background color of active tab.

items.name: Custom Cursor extension
items.summary: Adds a custom cursor to pages on https://developer.chrome.com. This sample is part of a tutorial on YouTube.

items.name: Focus Mode
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to use the Scripting API to inject and remove CSS on demand, enabling a distraction-free reading experience on Chrome's documentation pages.

items.name: Oliver Focus Mode
items.summary: Extension used in the Debugging Chrome extensions DevTools Tips video. This extension simplifies the styling of the extensions and Chrome Web Store documentation pages so that they are easier to read when the action icon is clicked.

items.name: Getting Started With Google Chrome Extensions
items.summary: This is an extension used in the [Debug extensions][1] tutorial. It changes the HTML body background color of the active tab. The purpose of this extension is to demonstrate how to create a simple Chrome Extension that uses the default_popup, options_page and service_worker manifest keys and…

items.name: Google Analytics 4 example
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to track extension events in Google Analytics 4 using the Measurement Protocol.

items.name: Getting Started With Google Chrome Extensions (Hello World)
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to create a simple "Hello World" Chrome Extension. For more details, visit the official tutorial.

items.name: Mole Game
items.summary: This mole game is based on a YouTube tutorial in our Chrome Extensions series. Watch it here.

items.name: Open Extension API Reference
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to use the Omnibox API to quickly navigate to Chrome extension API reference pages directly from the address bar.

items.name: Tutorial: Testing Chrome Extensions with Puppeteer
items.summary: This is the sample code for the Testing Chrome Extensions with Puppeteer tutorial.

items.name: Tutorial: Handling events
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to handle events with service workers.

items.name: Tutorial: Run scripts on every page
items.summary: This sample demonstrates how to run scripts on any Chrome extension and Chrome Web Store documentation page using an extension called _Reading Time_.

items.name: Tab Manager For Chrome Dev Docs
items.summary: This Chrome extension helps you manage and group your tabs related to Google Chrome Developer documentation. It organizes tabs into a group titled "DOCS" for easier navigation and enhanced productivity.

items.name: Testing service worker termination
items.summary: Note: The test extension is intentionally broken as part of a tutorial in our documentation. See Test service worker termination with Puppeteer.

items.name: Chrome extension WebSocket example
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to use WebSockets in a MV3 Chrome Extension. Starting with Chrome version M116, WebSocket activity will extend the service worker lifetime. In previous Chrome versions, the service worker will become inactive while waiting for messages and disconnect the WebSocket.
